analysis: The only change is in the test file GLM5NextLocalLoadPolicyTests.swift, line 614. The test stub OtherFamilyStubModel.prepare signature moves from (input, cache, windowSize) to (input, cache, state: LMOutput.State?, prefill: PrefillParameters). This tracks an upstream MLXLMCommon LanguageModel protocol change. The stub body is unchanged: it returns .tokens(input.text). It sits in test-only code, so it ships no production behavior. It adds no network, crypto, key, attestation, authorization or cache-storage logic. The surrounding test content covers GLM5Next local qualification, MTP gating, default-on prefix cache policy (T-041), and retained-fault handling. All of it is identical between base and head. The environment handling in GLM5NextStandaloneHost still sets DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 and the isolated cache root, so the tests do not touch the live KEK or cache. The PR text I was given does not show the matching production LanguageModel protocol or dependency bump, so I could not check it against this signature. Only the test stub changed here. I identified no security regression and no threat-model gap from the supplied evidence.
